comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C31-C35, C50. Both evaluations find the CaMKII phosphorylation effects on synGAP-PDZ binding convincingly supported by experimental evidence. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple assays; peer reviewers describe findings as 'very convincing' and 'largely solid.'

Strong disagreement on claims C46-C49, C51-C52, C89-C91 regarding S1283 phosphorylation. OpenEval finds mutational analysis data supporting the cumulative phosphorylation model. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about functional significance of S1283 (an in vitro site), question why S1123/S1283 double mutant wasn't tested, and request functional studies showing redistribution effects.

Agreement on claims C62-C64. Both evaluations support the Ca2+/CaM selective effect on PDZ3 binding. OpenEval notes functional significance remains unclear; peer reviewers accept findings as part of the overall activity-dependent regulation mechanism without specific challenge.

Disagreement on claims C6, C65-C69 regarding synGAP+/- PSD data. OpenEval finds the competition model supported though acknowledges alternative explanations exist. Peer reviewers express uncertainty due to potential developmental compensation effects and request critical discussion of alternative possibilities beyond the proposed model.

Disagreement on claims C78, C96-C98 regarding broader model implications. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting predictions extend beyond direct evidence and causal links to pathology are speculative. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, describing the model as 'beautifully logical and well-supported' and 'a substantially new way of looking at the PSD' with significant field influence.

Disagreement on claims C39-C43 regarding SPR-derived KD values. OpenEval finds the competition assay method appropriate and values internally consistent. Peer reviewer #3 expresses uncertainty about curve fitting methodology, notes curves don't fit data well, and requests consideration of alternative equations for accurate KD determination.

Agreement on claims C53-C57 regarding Ca2+/CaM binding to synGAP. Both evaluations support the direct binding evidence. OpenEval emphasizes Ca2+-dependent binding and substrate-specific phosphorylation enhancement. Peer reviewers accept Ca2+/CaM findings as part of overall mechanism without specific challenge.

Agreement on claims C5, C37 regarding PLK2 phosphorylation effects. Both evaluations support the kinase specificity data. OpenEval notes C38 (shared phosphorylation sites) supported by prior citations. Peer reviewers show interest in comparative kinase data and don't challenge PLK2 findings.

Agreement on claims C58-C61 regarding high-affinity Ca2+/CaM binding site localization. Both evaluations support the evidence from SPR and bead-binding measurements. OpenEval emphasizes localization to C-terminal region; peer reviewers accept as part of overall Ca2+/CaM mechanism.

Agreement on claim C36 regarding CDK5 phosphorylation specificity. Both evaluations support the negative control data showing no significant binding change. OpenEval emphasizes this as evidence for kinase specificity; peer reviewers accept kinase comparison data without challenge.

Partial overlap on claims C44-C45 regarding phosphorylation and S1283D mutation effects. OpenEval finds converging evidence from SPR measurements. Peer reviewer #3's concerns about KD determination methodology (R4) apply to these measurements as well, creating uncertainty about precise affinity values.

Agreement on claims C20-C26 regarding synGAP isoform expression and α1 abundance. Both evaluations support these prior findings as established context. Peer reviewer #3 emphasizes importance of distinguishing isoforms and confirms α1-containing synGAPs are abundantly expressed at synapses.

Agreement on claims C16-C18 regarding prior work on CaMKII-dependent synGAP dispersal (Araki et al.). Both evaluations accept these as established context. Peer reviewers acknowledge qualitative findings from prior work provide same bottom line regarding phosphorylation effects on PSD-95 interaction.

Partial overlap on claim C2 regarding synGAP binding capacity. OpenEval (R12) finds quantitative estimates reasonable given assumptions about protein abundance. Peer reviewers (R8) focus on broader model implications rather than specific binding capacity calculations, accepting overall framework.

OpenEval finds claim C81 (Ca2+/CaM binding doesn't affect GAP activity) supported by control data in Figure 8 supplement 2. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific control experiment.

OpenEval finds claims C1, C7-C9, C79-C80, C84-C88 (background knowledge about synGAP function, PSD composition, and synaptic plasticity) supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval rates claim C95 (synGAP as Ca2+/CaM buffer speculation) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's explicitly labeled as speculation and lacks direct experimental test. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific speculative claim.
